editorial:
Imagine two friends heading out to the middle of nowhere in Virginia just to make some music. You have Joe, who is dreaming of becoming a rap star, and Max, who wants to make a name for himself as a director. At first, the whole thing feels like a fun, lighthearted project. You get to see them joking around in a quiet house, trying to get the perfect sound for a demo CD. It feels like a typical buddy trip where everything is easy and the goals are simple. However, the mood shifts quickly as you realize something is very wrong with Joe.

What makes this stand out is how it switches from a comedy to something much darker. You watch Joe fight with a second personality that tries to ruin his life, and it feels scary because it is shot like a real home movie. Some parts might feel a bit slow, but the tension keeps you glued to the screen. If you like stories about people losing control, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a shocking realization about Joe's mental state. You see that the second personality, the fiend, has almost completely taken over his mind. Joe tries to fight back to regain control, but the battle is brutal. In the final scenes, it becomes clear that Joe cannot simply wish the alter-ego away. The story wraps up on a sad note, showing that some internal battles are nearly impossible to win alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage style movies and psychological dramas.
